safety.message: Red-flag questions were not answered, so urgent warning signs were not checked.
safety.note: This check runs separately from the model: a low model score never overrides it.

body.disclaimer: This is NOT a medical diagnosis. It is a research prototype trained on a small public dataset of 366 patients. Please see a doctor or dermatologist for any skin problem.
body.accuracyWarning: Many answers are missing; results are much less reliable.

predictions.label: Other scaly rash (lichen planus, pityriasis rosea or pityriasis rubra pilaris)

body.scoreNote: Scores sum to 1 across the four groups. They are NOT calibrated real-world probabilities, and can be extreme (near 0 or 1) when the answers match a typical pattern in the training data; that is not certainty.

explanation.method: exact linear contributions of the logistic-regression model (log-score, centred across conditions)

reasons.question: Is your scalp affected?
reasons.text: Your answer "severe" for scalp involvement raises the score for Psoriasis (strong).

reasons.question: Do the patches have sharp, clearly defined edges?
reasons.text: Your answer "none" for sharp edges lowers the score for Psoriasis (moderate).

reasons.question: Are your knees or elbows affected?
reasons.text: Your answer "none" for knee/elbow involvement lowers the score for Psoriasis (moderate).

reasons.question: How old are you (in years)?
reasons.text: Your answer "52 years" for your age raises the score for Psoriasis (small).

reasons.question: How much dry flaking or scaling is there on the patches?
reasons.text: Your answer "moderate" for flaking/scaling raises the score for Psoriasis (small).

reasons.question: How red is the affected skin?
reasons.text: Your answer "mild" for redness lowers the score for Psoriasis (small).

explanation.unsureAnswersNote: Questions marked 'not sure' were filled with the typical training value; their combined effect is shown here, not in the list.
explanation.strengthNote: strong / moderate / small = size relative to the biggest effect in this list (a display choice, not a medical grade).
explanation.scope: This shows how each answer moved this model's score for the condition, compared with an average patient in the training data. It explains the model only - it does not prove cause or confirm a diagnosis.

familyHistory.note: Share of training patients who had a family history, per group (real data). In this dataset it was far more common in psoriasis than in the other groups; it is not a hereditary-risk estimate for you.

limitations: Trained on the real UCI Dermatology dataset (366 patients, donated to UCI in 1998, single source). It may not represent you.
The dataset's features were scored by clinicians; your own answers may differ, and this has never been validated.
Only four outcome groups exist. Eczema subtypes such as atopic or contact dermatitis, and vitiligo, are NOT covered by this dataset.
Scores are model outputs, not calibrated real-world probabilities. Hiding answers ('not sure') lowers accuracy a lot.
nextSteps: Show this to a doctor or dermatologist - a clinician (sometimes with a biopsy) must confirm any diagnosis.
See a doctor soon if the rash is painful, spreading fast, blistering, infected, or comes with fever.
